lines.t: In this town, the sun never comes up. And nobody has ever seen a single light.
No lamps. No candles. Not even a match. The Mayor banned them all, a hundred years ago.
So Benny brushes his teeth in the dark. The baker bakes in the dark.
And Grandma knits in the dark... which is not going well.
And the dog walks into the same tree. Every. Single. Morning.
But one night, a girl named Pip finds something weird in her attic.
A tiny candle. And it's smirking at her.
She touches the wick. Fwoosh!
Her fingers start to glow.
She taps her old lantern. Boom! It lights up.
Her cat walks by. Now the cat glows too. He is not happy about it.
She runs outside and high-fives Benny. Whoosh! Now his whole hoodie is shining.
Benny touches the bakery window, and every loaf glows like gold.
Grandma's knitting lights up. Turns out, she knitted a sock... for a horse.
Then the street lamps. Pop. Pop. Pop. Pop!
But then, the doors of the town hall slam open.
Lights are against the rules! Turn them off. Right now!
And the Mayor starts blowing out every lamp, one by one. The street goes dark again.
Everyone freezes. Pip looks down at the little candle.
And the candle whispers just two words. Light the clock.
So Pip climbs the clock tower. Two hundred steps. In total darkness.
Halfway up, her hand starts to flicker. The light is running out.
She presses her glowing hand on the giant clock.
Boom! The clock blazes. The light rolls over every roof, every street, all the way to the hills.
And for the first time ever, the sky turns orange. The sun comes up.
The whole town cheers. Except the Mayor.
Because when the Mayor takes off his hat, there's a tiny lamp hidden inside.
He was never against the light. He just didn't want to share it.
And the little candle? He smirks, says see you tomorrow night, and blows himself out.
